_about: PunePedia source register. Every source an entry cites must be listed here. 'consulted' = true only when a PunePedia editor actually read this source. Sources marked consulted:false are recorded because a consulted source cites them; they are research directions, not checked evidence. 'reliability' is an editorial evaluation, not a property of the publisher's name.

sources.title: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, Vol. XVIII, Part I: Poona
sources.author: Government of Bombay (ed. James M. Campbell)
sources.reliability: Colonial-era official compilation. Valuable for 19th-century descriptions and for the sources it cites, but its readings of early history and local tradition must be checked against later scholarship. Located in the Internet Archive; not yet read for any entry.

sources.title: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, Vol. XVIII, Part II: Poona
sources.author: Government of Bombay (ed. James M. Campbell)
sources.reliability: As for Part I. Contains the district history chapters. Not yet read for any entry.

sources.title: Gazetteer of the Bombay Presidency, Vol. XVIII, Part III: Poona
sources.author: Government of Bombay (ed. James M. Campbell)
sources.reliability: Only the printed contents were checked: Chapter XIV 'Places' begins at p. 102, and the Poona city account sits inside that chapter. The city account itself has not yet been read; page references for individual places still need to be taken from the scan. The Maharashtra Gazetteers Department HTML edition blocks automated access and must be read manually.

sources.title: Gazetteer of Bombay State (Revised Edition), District Series Vol. XX: Poona District
sources.author: Government of Bombay
sources.reliability: Revised post-independence edition. Useful for comparison with the 1885 text. Not yet read.

sources.title: Urbanization of Pune: How Its Ground Was Prepared
sources.author: Kantak, M. R.
sources.publisher: Bulletin of the Deccan College Research Institute, vol. 51/52, pp. 489–495
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed regional history journal; the strongest available lead for the copper-plate references and the 1630–31 destruction of Pune. Must be read directly before its claims are treated as checked.

sources.title: The Religious Complex in Eighteenth-Century Poona
sources.author: Gokhale, Balkrishna Govind
sources.publisher: Journal of the American Oriental Society, vol. 105, no. 4, pp. 719–724
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed. Cited (p. 719) for Shahaji choosing Pune as the residence of Jijabai and Shivaji. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Poona: A Socio-Economic Survey, Part I
sources.author: Gadgil, D. R.
sources.publisher: Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics, Poona
sources.reliability: Classic survey by a major economist. Cited (p. 13) for an early-14th-century defensive wall. Held in the GIPE digital repository; not yet read.

sources.title: History of Pune
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article, editable by anyone. Used as a finding aid and for the scholarly citations it carries. Several statements on this page carry no footnote (for example the 1858 municipality date), and it disagrees with the 'Pune' article on the dynasty behind the earliest copper plates.

sources.title: Pune
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Its etymology section lists several name forms and inscription dates (758/768, 858/868 and 937 CE) and attributes the 758/768 plates to the Yadavas, which conflicts with other accounts. Most of these statements carry no visible footnote. Treat as a list of claims to check, not as evidence.

sources.title: Shaniwar Wada
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Construction dates are given precisely; the fire of 1828 is footnoted only to a 2015 Rediff feature, and the murder of Narayanrao only to newspaper and popular sources. The page gives no coordinates.

sources.title: The Era of Bajirao
sources.author: Kulkarni, Uday S.
sources.reliability: Narrative history by a Pune historian using Marathi records. Cited at p. 133 for the artisans of Shaniwar Wada. Not yet read directly; edition and year to be taken from the copy consulted.

sources.title: Lal Mahal
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article whose footnotes are mostly newspaper reports. The 1630 construction date and the 1984–1988 reconstruction are given; the original site's exact position is stated to be unknown.

sources.title: Pataleshwar
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article with good 19th-century architectural sources. The 8th-century / Rashtrakuta dating is stated but not tied to a specific footnote.

sources.title: The Cave Temples of India
sources.author: Fergusson, James; Burgess, James
sources.reliability: Foundational survey; cited at pp. 426–427 for the description of the Pataleshwar cave. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Notes on the Cave of Panchalesvara in Mouje Bhamburde, Taluka Haveli, Zilla Puna
sources.author: Sinclair, W. H.
sources.reliability: Early survey note. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Parvati Hill
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Gives coordinates 18°29′50″N 73°50′48″E. Inconsistent on the number of steps (103 in the infobox, 108 in the text), so neither figure is used here.

sources.title: The hill temples of the Peshwas
sources.author: Kulkarni, Uday S.
sources.reliability: Newspaper column by a historian. Cited for the 1749 completion of the Devdeveshwar temple and the 1760 gold pinnacle. Original article URL to be recovered.

sources.title: Aga Khan Palace
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Gives coordinates 18.5523°N, 73.9015°E. The 1892 construction year appears in the infobox without a footnote.

sources.title: Aga Khan Palace, Pune
sources.author: Gandhi Heritage Portal
sources.publisher: Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust, Ahmedabad
sources.reliability: Curated heritage portal run by a Gandhian memorial trust. Gives the death dates of Mahadev Desai and Kasturba Gandhi, Gandhi's release date and the 1969 gift. Does not give the construction year.

sources.title: History (About BORI)
sources.author: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute
sources.reliability: The institute's own chronology. Reliable for its own founding and project dates; read with ordinary institutional caution.

sources.title: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Used only for the address (812 Chiplunkar Road, Shivajinagar) and coordinates 18.51953°N, 73.82996°E.

sources.title: Bharat Itihas Sanshodhak Mandal
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Founding date footnoted to a 2021 Hindustan Times report. Collection figures are large round numbers and are not repeated here.

sources.title: Bharat Itihas Sanshodhak Mandal in Pune to digitise 250K rare documents
sources.author: Bengrut, Dheeraj
sources.reliability: Newspaper report. Exact article URL to be recovered.

sources.title: Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Founding date footnoted to an archived copy of the college website. The Vishrambaug Wada location and the 1864/1868 dates carry no footnote on this page.

sources.title: Deccan College website (archived)
sources.author: Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute
sources.publisher: Deccan College, Pune (Internet Archive capture of 23 May 2017)
sources.reliability: The institution's own account. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Deccan College: A Retrospect, 1851–1901
sources.author: Frazer, James Nelson
sources.reliability: Contemporary institutional history. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Battle of Khadki
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article with 19th-century military sources. Internally inconsistent in places (the lead names a different Maratha leader from the infobox; one reference gives the year 1816). Force sizes and casualty numbers are not repeated here.

sources.title: A History of the Mahrattas, Vol. 3
sources.author: Grant Duff, James
sources.publisher: Longman, Rees, Orme, Brown, and Green, London
sources.reliability: Written by a British official who served as Resident at Satara; important but partisan. Cited at pp. 406–454 for the 1817 campaign. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Vishrambaug Wada
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article footnoted to newspaper and tourism pages. Gives coordinates 18.52028, 73.85667. The 1930 purchase price is marked 'citation needed' there and is not used.

sources.title: Kasba Ganapati
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article footnoted to newspapers. Mixes tradition and history; several origin details are uncited. Gives coordinates 18°31′08″N 73°51′25″E.

sources.title: Poona Pact
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article with good scholarly references but internal inconsistencies about signatories and seat counts. Only the date and place are used here.

sources.title: Gandhi, Ambedkar and the Poona Pact, 1932
sources.author: Kumar, Ravinder
sources.publisher: South Asia: Journal of South Asian Studies, vol. 8, nos. 1–2, pp. 87–101
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed. Not yet read directly. Stable link (DOI or JSTOR) still to be recorded; URL points to the page that cites it.

sources.title: Yerwada Central Jail
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article. Gives Gandhi's fast as beginning 20 September 1932. The 1871 construction year is footnoted only to a newspaper and a city website.

sources.title: Satyashodhak Samaj
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article with strong scholarly references (O'Hanlon, Omvedt).

sources.title: Caste, Conflict, and Ideology: Mahatma Jotirao Phule and Low Caste Protest in Nineteenth-Century Western India
sources.author: O'Hanlon, Rosalind
sources.reliability: Standard scholarly monograph on Phule. Cited at pp. 220–251. Not yet read directly; stable publisher link still to be recorded. URL points to the page that cites it.

sources.title: Supreme Court allows national memorial to commemorate first girls' school in India
sources.author: Thanawala, Sarah
sources.reliability: Legal news site. Reliable for the litigation outcome; its historical statement (school opened 1848) is a summary, not primary evidence.

sources.title: Pune Municipal Corporation
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Gives 15 February 1950, footnoted to a Hindustan Times feature. Gives 1857 for the earlier municipality without a footnote, which conflicts with 1858 on the 'History of Pune' page.

sources.title: 68 years of Pune Municipal Corporation: Civic history with a legacy of game-changing schemes
sources.author: Hindustan Times
sources.reliability: Newspaper feature. Exact article URL to be recovered; a PMC or state gazette notification would be the better source.

sources.title: Fergusson College
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article citing the college's own history pages and Karve (1961). Gives coordinates 18.523969, 73.839219.

sources.title: The Deccan Education Society
sources.author: Karve, D. D.
sources.publisher: The Journal of Asian Studies, vol. 20, no. 2, pp. 205–212
sources.reliability: Peer-reviewed, written by a scholar associated with the Society. Not yet read directly.

sources.title: Row over history of Pune's community Ganesh festival
sources.author: Press Trust of India
sources.reliability: Wire report that sets out both sides of the dispute and the evidence each side cites. Reports the dispute; does not settle it.

sources.title: 60 Years of Ganeshotsav
sources.author: Karandikar, J. S.
sources.reliability: Cited by the Pune mayor in 2017 in support of the 1893 date. Title as reported in English; original Marathi title, publisher and pages not yet identified. URL points to the report that cites it.

sources.title: Panshet Dam
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article footnoted to newspapers and the Central Water Commission register. Gives dam coordinates 18.37972, 73.61111. Its death-toll estimate rests on a newspaper retrospective and is not repeated here.

sources.title: Prime Minister inaugurates Pune Metro Rail (press release)
sources.author: Maharashtra Metro Rail Corporation Ltd (Maha Metro)
sources.reliability: Operator's own release, hosted on its website (issuer not printed on the document). Gives 6 March 2022 and two opened sections: PCMC–Phugewadi (7 km) and Garware–Vanaz (5 km). It mislabels the Garware–Vanaz section's corridor.

sources.title: Shinde Chhatri
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article citing Moledina's cantonment history (1953) and newspapers. Gives no coordinates.

sources.title: History of the Poona Cantonment, 1818–1953
sources.author: Moledina, M. H.
sources.reliability: Local institutional history. Publisher and pages not yet identified; URL points to the page that cites it.

sources.title: Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability: Encyclopaedia article; gives both 1920 (start of collecting) and 1962 (museum established), which are different events. Gives no coordinates.

sources.title: Will razed Lal Mahal rise from the rubble?
sources.author: The Times of India
sources.reliability: Newspaper report cited for the destruction of the original building. URL points to the page that cites it; archived original to be recovered.
